chapters.1.lds: The 2023 lesson studies Joseph’s response and faith in Jesus, the Son of God. Why does the family list change its wording when it reaches Joseph and Mary?
chapters.1.summary: Matthew opens with the family line of Jesus Christ, son of David and Abraham. It runs in three sets of fourteen generations. Four women appear in it: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and Uriah’s wife. Mary is pledged to Joseph and is found with child by the Holy Spirit. Joseph plans to end the engagement quietly. An angel tells him in a dream to take Mary as his wife. The child will be named Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins. Joseph does as he is told.
chapters.2.lds: Why does Matthew keep the other children’s deaths beside the child’s escape?
chapters.2.summary: Wise men from the east come to Jerusalem seeking the newborn king of the Jews. King Herod is troubled and learns the Christ should be born in Bethlehem. The star leads the wise men to the child, and they worship him with gifts. A dream warns them not to return to Herod. An angel tells Joseph to flee to Egypt with the child and his mother. Herod kills the young boys of Bethlehem. After Herod dies, Joseph brings the family back. They settle in Nazareth in Galilee.
chapters.3.lds: Why does John demand visible fruit rather than claims about ancestry?
chapters.3.summary: John the Baptist preaches in the desert of Judea. He tells people to repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is near. He wears camel’s hair and eats locusts and wild honey. Crowds come and are baptized in the Jordan, confessing their sins. He warns the Pharisees and Sadducees to bear fruit that fits repentance. They must not rely on having Abraham as their father. Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized. The Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice calls him God’s beloved Son.
chapters.4.lds: How does the second temptation show that quoting Scripture alone cannot settle the dispute?
chapters.4.summary: The Spirit leads Jesus into the desert, where he fasts forty days. The devil tells him to turn stones into bread. He tells him to throw himself from the temple and trust the angels. He offers all the world’s kingdoms in return for worship. Jesus answers each time from Deuteronomy. He then begins to preach in Galilee. He calls four fishermen, who leave their nets and follow him. He heals the sick, and great crowds gather.
chapters.5.lds: The selected 2023 lesson studies blessed lives and reads completeness through Christ. Why must repairing the relationship come before completing the offering?
chapters.5.summary: Jesus goes up a mountain and teaches his disciples. He calls the poor in spirit, the mourners, and the merciful blessed. His followers are salt and light. He has come to fulfill the law, not to destroy it. Anger and insult are judged along with murder. He speaks about lust, divorce, oaths, and revenge. He tells them to love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them. They are to be complete, as their Father is.
chapters.6.lds: How do public admiration and stored treasure place competing claims on the heart?
chapters.6.summary: Jesus warns against doing good in order to be seen. Giving, prayer, and fasting should be done in secret before the Father. He gives his disciples a prayer to use. They must forgive others as they ask to be forgiven. They should store treasure in heaven and not on earth. No one can serve two masters. They should not be anxious about food or clothing. They should seek God’s Kingdom first.
chapters.7.lds: What separates the two builders when both hear the same teaching?
chapters.7.summary: Jesus warns against judging others while ignoring one’s own faults. He tells his hearers to ask, seek, and knock. They should treat others as they want to be treated. The gate to life is narrow. False prophets are known by their fruit. Not everyone who calls him Lord will enter the Kingdom. The one who hears and acts is like a house built on rock. The crowds are amazed at his authority.
chapters.8.lds: Why does the officer describe his own authority when asking Jesus for help?
chapters.8.summary: Jesus comes down from the mountain and heals a man with a skin disease. A Roman officer asks him to heal a paralyzed servant. The officer says Jesus need only speak the word. Jesus marvels at his faith and heals the servant. He heals Peter’s mother-in-law and many others. He warns would-be followers of the cost. He calms a storm on the lake. Across the water he frees two men from demons, and the town sends him away.
chapters.9.lds: How does the physician comparison answer criticism of the shared meal?
chapters.9.summary: Jesus forgives and heals a paralyzed man, and scribes accuse him of blasphemy. He calls Matthew, a tax collector, who follows him. He eats with tax collectors and sinners, and Pharisees object. He says the sick are the ones who need a doctor. He raises a ruler’s daughter and heals a woman who touches his cloak. He gives sight to two blind men and speech to a mute man. He has compassion on the crowds, who are like sheep without a shepherd. He tells his disciples to pray for workers.
chapters.10.lds: What makes receiving a traveling disciple part of receiving Jesus?
chapters.10.summary: Jesus calls twelve disciples and gives them authority to heal. He sends them to the lost sheep of Israel. They must give freely, as they have freely received. They carry no money or extra clothes and stay with those who welcome them. They will be arrested and hated for his name. They should not fear those who can kill only the body. Family members will turn against each other. Whoever receives them receives Jesus.
chapters.11.lds: Why does Jesus answer John with acts of healing and good news?
chapters.11.summary: John the Baptist is in prison and hears what Jesus is doing. He sends disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one to come. Jesus tells them to report what they see and hear. He praises John as more than a prophet. He says this generation is like children who are never satisfied. He rebukes towns that saw his works and did not repent. He thanks the Father for showing these things to little children. He invites the weary to come and find rest.
chapters.12.lds: How does the hungry disciples’ situation shape the Sabbath argument?
chapters.12.summary: The disciples pick grain on the Sabbath because they are hungry. Pharisees say this is unlawful. Jesus recalls that David ate holy bread when he was hungry. He heals a man’s withered hand in the synagogue. The Pharisees plan to destroy him. He frees a blind and mute man, and they credit the ruler of demons. He answers that a divided kingdom cannot stand. He says whoever does his Father’s will is his family.
chapters.13.lds: Why does the owner stop servants from removing the weeds immediately?
chapters.13.summary: Jesus teaches the crowds from a boat with stories. A farmer sows seed on four kinds of soil. An enemy sows weeds among a man’s wheat. The Kingdom is like a mustard seed and like yeast in flour. It is like hidden treasure, a fine pearl, and a net full of fish. He explains the stories to his disciples in private. He goes to his home town, and the people take offense. He does few mighty works there.
chapters.14.lds: What does each meal show about the person who directs it?
chapters.14.summary: Herod the ruler hears about Jesus and thinks he is John risen from the dead. Herod had jailed John for condemning his marriage. At his birthday feast a girl’s dance pleases him, and he promises her anything. She asks for John’s head, and he gives the order. Jesus withdraws, and crowds follow him. He feeds five thousand men with five loaves and two fish. He walks on the sea to his disciples at night. Peter steps out, sinks, and is caught by Jesus.
chapters.15.lds: How does the woman’s reply use the same image that excludes her?
chapters.15.summary: Pharisees ask why the disciples do not wash their hands before eating. Jesus says they set aside God’s command for their tradition. What comes out of the mouth defiles a person, not what goes in. He travels to the region of Tyre and Sidon. A Canaanite woman begs him to heal her daughter. He says he was sent to Israel, and she keeps asking. He praises her faith and heals the girl. Back in Galilee he heals many and feeds four thousand.
chapters.16.lds: Doctrine and Covenants 128:10 quotes verses 18–19 about binding on earth. Why can Peter confess Jesus’ identity and still oppose his announced path?
chapters.16.summary: Pharisees and Sadducees ask Jesus for a sign from heaven. He warns his disciples about their teaching. He asks the disciples who they say he is. Peter answers that he is the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus blesses him and speaks of building his assembly. Then he says he must suffer, be killed, and rise. Peter rebukes him, and Jesus calls him a stumbling block. Anyone who follows him must take up a cross.
chapters.17.lds: How does the suffering discussed afterward change the meaning of the mountain scene?
chapters.17.summary: Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. His face shines like the sun, and Moses and Elijah appear with him. Peter offers to build three shelters. A bright cloud covers them, and a voice calls Jesus the beloved Son. The disciples fall down afraid, and Jesus touches them. He tells them to say nothing until he has risen. Below, he heals a boy the disciples could not heal. He again says he will be killed and raised.
chapters.18.lds: The selected 2023 lesson connects receiving forgiveness with forgiving others. Why does the king ask the forgiven debtor about mercy toward his fellow servant?
chapters.18.summary: The disciples ask who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven. Jesus sets a child among them and tells them to become like children. He warns against causing little ones to stumble. A shepherd leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one that strayed. He teaches how to deal with a brother who sins. Peter asks how often he must forgive. Jesus tells of a servant forgiven a huge debt. That servant jails a man who owes him little and is punished.
chapters.19.lds: What does the young man’s sorrow reveal about the demand Jesus makes?
chapters.19.summary: Pharisees test Jesus with a question about divorce. He points them to the beginning, when God joined man and woman. People bring children, and he blesses them. A rich young man asks what good thing he must do to have eternal life. He says he has kept the commandments. Jesus tells him to sell what he has and give to the poor. The young man goes away sad. Jesus says the last will be first.
chapters.20.lds: Why do the earlier workers resent receiving exactly the wage they agreed upon?
chapters.20.summary: Jesus tells of a landowner who hires workers at dawn for a day’s wage. He hires more at later hours, even an hour before sunset. At evening each receives the same wage. Those hired first complain. Jesus again foretells his death and resurrection. The mother of James and John asks for the best seats for her sons. Jesus says the great must be servants. He gives sight to two blind men near Jericho.
chapters.21.lds: Whom does the chapter identify as the immediate hearers of the vineyard accusation?
chapters.21.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey, and crowds shout “Hosanna.” He drives the traders out of the temple and heals there. The chief priests ask by what authority he acts. He answers with a question about John’s baptism. He tells of two sons, only one of whom obeys. He tells of tenants who kill the owner’s servants and then his son. He says the Kingdom will be given to others. The leaders want to arrest him and fear the crowds.
chapters.22.lds: How does the answer about love hold the law’s different demands together?
chapters.22.summary: Jesus tells of a king whose invited guests refuse his son’s wedding feast. The Pharisees ask whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar. He says to give Caesar what is Caesar’s and God what is God’s. The Sadducees ask about marriage in the resurrection. He says God is the God of the living. A lawyer asks which commandment is greatest. Jesus names love for God and love for neighbor. He then asks how the Christ can be David’s son and David’s Lord.
chapters.23.lds: Why does the spice tithe example place small obedience beside neglected justice?
chapters.23.summary: Jesus speaks to the crowds and his disciples about the scribes and Pharisees. They teach the law and do not practice it. They load others with heavy burdens and love titles and honor. He pronounces a series of woes on them. They shut the Kingdom against people. They tithe small herbs and neglect justice, mercy, and faith. They are like whitewashed tombs. He grieves over Jerusalem, which kills the prophets.
chapters.24.lds: Joseph Smith—Matthew gives Joseph Smith’s translation of this chapter. What distinguishes the faithful servant’s conduct during the delay?
chapters.24.summary: Jesus says the temple’s stones will all be thrown down. On the Mount of Olives his disciples ask when and what the sign will be. He warns of false christs, wars, famines, and persecution. They must flee when they see the desolating sacrilege. The Son of Man will come like lightning. No one knows the day or hour, not even the angels. As in Noah’s days, people will be caught unaware. So they must watch and be ready.
chapters.25.lds: Why are both groups surprised by the king’s explanation of their treatment of him?
chapters.25.summary: Jesus tells of ten young women waiting with lamps for a bridegroom. Five run out of oil and are shut out. He tells of a man who entrusts money to three servants. Two put it to work, and one buries it. Then he describes the Son of Man on his throne. He separates people as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. Some fed the hungry, welcomed strangers, and visited prisoners. The King says they did it to him.
chapters.26.lds: How does Jesus’ rejection of the sword differ from the arresting crowd’s use of force?
chapters.26.summary: The chief priests plot to kill Jesus, and a woman anoints him with costly oil. Judas agrees to hand him over for thirty pieces of silver. Jesus eats the Passover with the twelve and gives them bread and the cup. Peter promises never to deny him. In Gethsemane Jesus prays while the disciples sleep. Judas arrives with an armed crowd, and Jesus is arrested. The council condemns him for blasphemy. Peter denies knowing him three times and weeps.
chapters.27.lds: How do Pilate’s actions differ from his public claim of innocence?
chapters.27.summary: Jesus is handed to Pilate, the governor. Judas returns the silver and hangs himself. Pilate questions Jesus and offers to release a prisoner. The crowd asks for Barabbas. Pilate washes his hands and says he is innocent of this blood. Soldiers mock Jesus with a robe, a crown of thorns, and a reed. He is crucified between two robbers and dies. Joseph of Arimathea buries him, and the tomb is sealed and guarded.
chapters.28.lds: The selected 2023 lesson teaches resurrection through the Gospel accounts. How does the closing promise connect with the opening name Immanuel?
chapters.28.summary: At dawn after the Sabbath two women come to the tomb. An angel rolls back the stone and tells them Jesus has risen. They run to tell the disciples and meet Jesus on the way. The guards are paid to say the body was stolen. The eleven go to a mountain in Galilee. They worship him, though some doubt. He says all authority has been given to him. He sends them to make disciples of all nations and promises to be with them.
